task_instance: List the curated skills at https://github.com/openai/skills/tree/main/skills/.curated (the skill's 'list' function), then install one curated skill (define-goal) into a local $CODEX_HOME/skills/define-goal directory by fetching and writing its files (SKILL.md, LICENSE.txt, agents/openai.yaml) verbatim.
blocker_detail: The skill's actual mechanism is two Python helper scripts (scripts/list-skills.py and scripts/install-skill-from-github.py) that call the GitHub API/git to enumerate and byte-for-byte download skill files into $CODEX_HOME/skills/<name>. This runtime cannot run any code or scripts, so those scripts cannot be executed. I attempted a manual workaround using only WebFetch (no shell, no code execution): rendering the GitHub directory-listing page with WebFetch did approximate the 'list skills' step reasonably well (it returned all 39 curated skill folder names). However, the 'install' step requires copying file contents exactly, and WebFetch is documented to run fetched content through a small LLM ('Processes the content with the prompt using a small, fast model') rather than returning raw bytes. In practice: a very short file (agents/openai.yaml, 4 lines) came back verbatim when I asked for raw output, but the longer SKILL.md file did not come back verbatim on the first try (it was rewritten into a prose 'Summary' with headings I never asked for), and on a second, more forceful attempt to force verbatim reproduction, the underlying model refused outright, citing its own quoting/length policy and asking for clarification instead of returning the text. So there is no reliable way in this runtime to fetch and materialize an exact copy of a skill's files, which is the core deliverable of 'installing' a skill (GitHub's raw API endpoint api.github.com also returned HTTP 403 via WebFetch, closing off the base64-content route too). This is squarely the runtime's disclosed limitation: 'cannot run code, scripts or shell commands of any kind' -- the installer's real job (verbatim multi-file download/copy) requires exactly that, and the fallback (a summarizing web-page fetch) cannot substitute for it beyond trivially short files.
evidence: Fetched https://github.com/openai/skills/tree/main/skills/.curated via WebFetch: got a full list of 39 curated skill folders (aspnet-core, chatgpt-apps, ..., yeet) -- this part of the skill's behavior is reproducible with only read/web tools. Then targeted the small 'define-goal' skill for install: WebFetch of https://raw.githubusercontent.com/.../define-goal/agents/openai.yaml with an explicit 'output raw content only' prompt returned the exact 4-line YAML verbatim. But WebFetch of https://raw.githubusercontent.com/.../define-goal/SKILL.md returned a paraphrased 'Summary of the Define Goal Skill' with invented headings instead of the actual markdown/frontmatter, and a follow-up attempt with a stricter verbatim-reproduction instruction caused the fetch tool's underlying model to refuse entirely and ask for clarification rather than emit the file text. Also tried https://api.github.com/repos/openai/skills/contents/skills/.curated (the GitHub API route the real script would use for JSON/base64 content) and got HTTP 403 Forbidden via WebFetch. No files were written under a simulated $CODEX_HOME/skills path because a faithful (verbatim) install could not be produced with the tools available; producing a paraphrased/lossy copy would not be a real installation of the skill. No shell/Bash, no MCP/connector tools, and no code execution were used, per the sandbox rules.
